basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 13.' and it opens 'VERS. 13.-- Homines autem Sodomitae pessimi erant, et peccatores coram Domino nimis.'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 13.-- Homines autem Sodomitae pessimi erant, et peccatores coram Domino nimis. Superflue | additum est, coram Domino, sicut in LXX etiam invenitur; siquidem Sodomorum coloni apud homines mali et peccatores erant. Ille autem dicitur in conspectu Dei peccator, qui potest apud homines justus videri, quomodo de Zacharia et Elisabeth in praeconio ponitur, quod fuerint justi ambo in conspectu Dei, et in psalmo dicitur: Non justificabitur in conspectu tuo omnis vivens (Psal. CXLII, 2).
